122	  - `CoachingPayload` value type (`metrics: [String: Double]`, `tags: [String]`) with a

142	cascade inverse would have *deleted* the memory when a plan is removed, the opposite of the intent.

180	## Iteration 4 — 2026-07-02 ~11:40 — Claude Fable 5 — Item B1
181	
182	**Item:** B1. Progression engine (deterministic core) — increase load / increase reps / hold /
183	deload with a reason, math in code, not the model.
184	
185	**What changed:**
186	- NEW `Replog/Domain/ProgressionEngine.swift` — pure double-progression rule table:
187	  - `ProgressionAction` (`increaseLoad`/`increaseReps`/`hold`/`deload`, `displayName`) and
188	    `ProgressionRecommendation` (`exId`, `action`, `suggestedWeightKg`, `suggestedReps`,
189	    one-sentence `reason` ready for the B2 log card / a B3 `CoachingLog`).
190	  - `recommend(exId:history:repRange:weightStepKg:units:)` — rules, first match wins:
191	    (1) bodyweight lift (topW 0) trends on **reps** (stored e1RM is weight-based, always 0)
192	    — +1 rep uncapped, or hold on a rep stall/regression, never a weight suggestion;
193	    (2) rep-range top reached → +1 weight step, reps reset to the range floor;
194	    (3) e1RM dropped 2 consecutive deltas → deload; (4) no e1RM improvement across
195	    3 deltas → plateau deload; (5) single down session → hold (noise, not a trend);
196	    (6) otherwise +1 rep (clamped into the range).
197	  - `deloadWeight(fromKg:stepKg:)` — ~10% off, snapped to the stepper increment, always
198	    strictly below the current weight, floored at 0.
199	  - `repRange(for goal:)` — 8–12 hypertrophy/recomp, 12–15 fat loss, 6–10 sport (brackets
200	    `PlanGenerator`'s fixed 10/13/8); goal+units convenience reuses `Formulas.weightStepKg`
201	    and formats reasons via `Formulas.formatWeight` in the user's display units.
202	- FIX `Replog/Models/Coaching.swift` — `CoachingPayload` is now `nonisolated`: a clean full
203	  build surfaced 2 Swift-6 warnings from iter 3 (MainActor-isolated Codable conformance used
204	  inside nonisolated JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder generics — the custom `init(from:)` suppressed
205	  the usual nonisolated synthesis). Behavior unchanged; all 14 CoachingLog tests still green.
206	- NEW `ReplogTests/ProgressionEngineTests.swift` — 21 tests: empty/single-session/order-
207	  invariance; progressing (+rep, range-top +load & reset, above-top, below-floor lift);
208	  priority (range top beats a regressing trail); off-day hold; 2-drop regression deload;
209	  4-session flat plateau deload; 3-session flat still pushes reps; dip-then-recovery is not
210	  a regression; bodyweight rep progression past the range top + bodyweight stall holds;
211	  deload snapping/strict-below (property-swept 2.5–200 kg)/zero-step/zero-weight; goal rep
212	  ranges bracket the generator prescription; goal convenience; lb step + lb-formatted reasons.
213	
214	**Build:** clean, 0 errors / 0 warnings (** BUILD SUCCEEDED **) — after fixing the two
215	pre-existing iter-3 warnings above.
216	**Tests:** 211/211 passed on iPhone 17 (was 190; +21, all logic-layer). Every rule branch,
217	both deload reasons, both bodyweight paths and all `deloadWeight` edges are exercised.
218	
219	**Screenshots:** none — pure Domain addition, no UI surface yet (that's B2).
220	
221	**Assumptions / decisions:**
222	1. **Double progression** is the model: reps climb at fixed weight; load rises only when the
223	   goal's rep-range top is hit (then reps reset to the floor). Thresholds as named constants:
224	   `regressionDeltas = 2` (e1RM strictly down), `plateauDeltas = 3` (no improvement),
225	   `deloadFactor = 0.9`.
226	2. **Hitting the range top beats a bad trend** — reaching the top IS current success even if
227	   prior sessions regressed (tested).
228	3. **Bodyweight lifts trend on reps, not e1RM** — stored e1RM is `weight × (1 + reps/30)` = 0
229	   at 0 kg, so an e1RM-based stall signal would mark ANY 4-session bodyweight trail a plateau.
230	   Caught by hand-verifying test expectations; rep-delta logic added. Bodyweight stalls hold
231	   (form/quality cue) rather than "deload" a weight that doesn't exist.
232	4. The engine is **per-lift and history-in, recommendation-out pure**; no CoachingLog writes
233	   (that wiring is B3's acceptance) and no windowing — callers pass the (already relevant)
234	   entries, matching `ProgressAggregator`'s contract.
235	5. A single down session recommends **hold**, not deload — one bad day is noise; the reason
236	   string says so.
237

321	## Iteration 6 — 2026-07-02 ~12:20 — Claude Fable 5 — Item B3
322	
323	**Item:** B3. Plateau + deload detection — detect stalls across sessions, recommend a
324	deload or exercise swap, and record the recommendation to `CoachingLog`.
325	
326	**What changed:**
327	- NEW `Replog/Domain/StallDetector.swift`:
328	  - `StallTrend` (`regression`/`plateau`), `StallResponse` (`deload`/`swapExercise`),
329	    `StallDetection` (exId, trend, response, `sessionsStalled`, `stallStartDate`,
330	    last top set + e1RM).
331	  - Pure `detect(exId:history:)` — reuses `ProgressionEngine`'s thresholds
332	    (2 strict declines → regression, 3 non-improving deltas → plateau) over the
333	    trailing run of the e1RM series; three refinements beyond B1:
334	    (a) a **latest-session back-off** (top weight down ≥5%, `backoffFraction`) returns
335	    nil — the user just deloaded, a rebuild in progress is not a stall;
336	    (b) **escalation**: a back-off earlier in the last `swapLookbackDeltas` (8) steps
337	    but *before* the current stalled run means a deload was already tried and didn't
338	    fix it → response is `swapExercise` instead of another deload (the run's own drops
339	    are excluded so a regression never counts as its own remedy);
340	    (c) **bodyweight lifts** stall on top reps (stored e1RM is 0) and always get
341	    `swapExercise` — there is no load to shed, change the stimulus.
342	  - Pure `swapCandidates(for:catalog:limit:)` — same equipment (guaranteed available)
343	    + same first primary muscle, ranked same-mechanic then same-level then name.
344	  - `detectAndRecord(exId:history:context:catalog:date:)` — the CoachingLog write:
345	    kind `.deload` (deload response, with `deloadToKg` via `ProgressionEngine.deloadWeight`
346	    in the user's display units) or `.plateau` (swap response, candidate exIds in tags,
347	    first candidate named in the summary); metrics carry `sessionsStalled`/last top set.
348	    **One memory per stall**: skips when the newest plateau/deload log for the lift is
349	    dated inside the current stall and carries the same response tag — a fresh stall or
350	    a deload→swap escalation records anew.
351	- `Replog/Domain/SessionFinisher.swift` — after each exercise's `HistoryEntry` insert,
352	  calls `StallDetector.detectAndRecord` with prior history + the new entry (prior is
353	  fetched before the insert, so no reliance on pending-changes fetch semantics).
354	  Signature unchanged; partial finishes also detect (a logged session is real evidence).
355	- NEW `ReplogTests/StallDetectorTests.swift` — 26 tests: too-little/progressing/single-dip
356	  nil cases; order invariance; plateau + regression detection with `sessionsStalled` and
357	  `stallStartDate`; three-flat-not-yet-plateau boundary; latest-back-off suppression;
358	  tried-deload escalation to swap; regression's own drops not counting as a tried deload;
359	  back-off older than the lookback not escalating; 3 bodyweight trend tests; 3

1	//
2	//  Coaching.swift
3	//  Replog
4	//
5	//  The trainer's durable memory. A `CoachingLog` is a dated, typed note the on-device
6	//  coach writes to itself — a progression recommendation, a detected plateau, a
7	//  bodyweight check-in, a published report — so it can "remember" context across weeks
8	//  and feed later reasoning (progression engine, weekly/monthly reports).
9	//
10	//  Like `HistoryEntry`, a log is a flat, queryable record: it references the catalog by
11	//  `exId` and a plan by `planId` (UUIDs, not relationships — matching `ActiveSession.workoutId`),
12	//  so the memory OUTLIVES the plan or exercise it once concerned. Structured detail rides
13	//  in a JSON payload, decoded on demand (the `HistoryEntry.sets` pattern).
14	//
15	
16	import Foundation
17	import SwiftData
18	
19	/// What a `CoachingLog` records. Drives filtering, iconography, and report grouping.
20	enum CoachingKind: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Identifiable, Sendable {
21	    /// A free-form coaching note.
22	    case note
23	    /// A load/rep recommendation for a specific lift (from the progression engine).
24	    case progression
25	    /// A detected stall across sessions.
26	    case plateau
27	    /// A recommended deload / back-off week.
28	    case deload
29	    /// A bodyweight check-in observation.
30	    case bodyweight
31	    /// A published weekly summary.
32	    case weeklyReport
33	    /// A published monthly rollup.
34	    case monthlyReport
35	    /// The coach adjusted the plan (split/volume/exercise choice).
36	    case planAdjustment
37	
38	    var id: String { rawValue }
39	
40	    var displayName: String {
41	        switch self {
42	        case .note:          return "Note"
43	        case .progression:   return "Progression"
44	        case .plateau:       return "Plateau"
45	        case .deload:        return "Deload"
46	        case .bodyweight:    return "Bodyweight"
47	        case .weeklyReport:  return "Weekly report"
48	        case .monthlyReport: return "Monthly report"
49	        case .planAdjustment: return "Plan adjustment"
50	        }
51	    }
52	}
53	
54	/// Structured detail for a `CoachingLog`, kept flexible so each `CoachingKind` can carry
55	/// only what it needs. Numeric facts (weights, e1RM, trend %, bodyweight) go in `metrics`;
56	/// short labels (recommended action verbs, muscle names) go in `tags`.
57	// Nonisolated: a pure value type whose Codable conformance must be usable inside the
58	// nonisolated JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder generics (the custom `init(from:)` would otherwise
59	// inherit the module's default MainActor isolation).
60	nonisolated struct CoachingPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
61	    /// Named numeric facts, e.g. `["fromWeightKg": 60, "toWeightKg": 62.5, "trendPct": 4.1]`.
62	    var metrics: [String: Double]
63	    /// Short labels, e.g. `["increaseLoad"]` or `["chest", "triceps"]`.
64	    var tags: [String]
65	
66	    init(metrics: [String: Double] = [:], tags: [String] = []) {
67	        self.metrics = metrics
68	        self.tags = tags
69	    }
70	
71	    /// Lenient decoding so a bare `{}` (the model's default `payloadJSON`) and forward-compatible
72	    /// payloads that omit a field decode to sensible empties instead of throwing.
73	    init(from decoder: any Decoder) throws {
74	        let c = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
75	        self.metrics = try c.decodeIfPresent([String: Double].self, forKey: .metrics) ?? [:]
76	        self.tags = try c.decodeIfPresent([String].self, forKey: .tags) ?? []
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Convenience metric accessor (nil when absent).
80	    subscript(metric key: String) -> Double? { metrics[key] }
81	}
82	
83	@Model
84	final class CoachingLog {
85	    var id: UUID = UUID()
86	    var date: Date = Date()
87	    /// Stored as `CoachingKind.rawValue`; use `kind` for typed access.
88	    var kindRaw: String = CoachingKind.note.rawValue
89	    /// Human-readable one-liner (rendered in reports / a future coaching feed).
90	    var summary: String = ""
91	    /// The exercise this log concerns (`Exercise.id` in the static catalog), if any.
92	    var exId: String?
93	    /// The plan this log concerns, if any. A plain id reference (not a relationship) so the
94	    /// memory survives the plan's deletion.
95	    var planId: UUID?
96	    /// JSON-encoded `CoachingPayload` of structured detail.
97	    var payloadJSON: String = "{}"
98	
99	    init(
100	        kind: CoachingKind,
101	        summary: String,
102	        date: Date = Date(),
103	        exId: String? = nil,
104	        planId: UUID? = nil,
105	        payload: CoachingPayload = CoachingPayload()
106	    ) {
107	        self.kindRaw = kind.rawValue
108	        self.summary = summary
109	        self.date = date
110	        self.exId = exId
111	        self.planId = planId
112	        self.payload = payload
113	    }
114	
115	    var kind: CoachingKind {
116	        get { CoachingKind(rawValue: kindRaw) ?? .note }
117	        set { kindRaw = newValue.rawValue }
118	    }
119	
120	    /// Decoded structured payload.
121	    var payload: CoachingPayload {
122	        get { (try? JSONDecoder().decode(CoachingPayload.self, from: Data(payloadJSON.utf8))) ?? CoachingPayload() }
123	        set { payloadJSON = String(data: (try? JSONEncoder().encode(newValue)) ?? Data("{}".utf8), encoding: .utf8) ?? "{}" }
124	    }
125	}

11

13	
14	    /// Renders a report + plan into reader-facing markdown.
15	    static func markdown(report: PlanReport, plan: GeneratedPlan) -> String {
16	        var out = "# \(plan.headline)\n\n"
17	        out += "\(report.philosophy)\n\n"
18	
19	        out += "## Why this split\n\(report.whyThisSplit)\n\n"
20	
21	        out += "## Your training week\n"

26	                out += "- **\(ex.name)** — \(ex.reason)\n"
27	            }
28	            out += "\n"
29	        }
30	
31	        out += "## The science\n\(report.scienceNotes)\n\n"
32	        out += "## Staying safe\n\(report.safetyNotes)\n\n"

38	    /// including a per-exercise breakdown (names derived from the catalog exercise ids).
39	    static func fallbackReport(answers: QuizAnswers, plan: GeneratedPlan) -> PlanReport {
40	        let name = answers.firstName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
41	        let greeting = name.isEmpty ? "" : "\(name), "
42	        let days = answers.daysPerWeek
43	        let goal = answers.goal.displayName.lowercased()
44	
45	        let philosophy =
46	            "\(greeting.capitalizedFirst)we built this plan around your goal to \(goal), training " +
47	            "\(days) day\(days == 1 ? "" : "s") a week as a \(answers.experience.displayName.lowercased()) lifter. " +
48	            "Every choice is grounded in exercise science — the aim is steady, sustainable progress " +
49	            "while respecting your recovery and your time."
50	
51	        let whyThisSplit =
52	            "We chose a \(plan.name) structure with \(plan.workouts.count) training day\(plan.workouts.count == 1 ? "" : "s"). " +
53	            "Grouping related muscles into the same session lets each muscle be trained hard, then " +
54	            "fully recover before its next session — research shows hitting each muscle roughly twice " +
55	            "a week maximizes muscle protein synthesis without overreaching."
56	
57	        let perDay = plan.workouts.map { workout -> PerDayNote in
58	            let notes = workout.items.enumerated().map { i, item in
59	                ExerciseNote(name: prettyName(item.exId), reason: fallbackReason(index: i))
60	            }
61	            return PerDayNote(
62	                dayName: workout.name,
63	                text: "These movements share a function, so synergists warm up and fatigue together " +
64	                      "and recover as a unit.",
65	                exercises: notes
66	            )
67	        }
68	
69	        let repWindow: String
70	        switch answers.goal {
71	        case .buildMuscle, .recomp: repWindow = "8-12 reps, the hypertrophy sweet spot"
72	        case .loseWeight: repWindow = "higher reps (12-15) to keep density and calorie burn up"
73	        case .sport: repWindow = "lower reps (6-8) to bias strength and power"
74	        }
75	        let scienceNotes =
76	            "Progress comes from progressive overload: add a little weight or a rep when a set feels " +
77	            "easier than your target RPE. We program \(repWindow), and use RPE (rate of perceived " +
78	            "exertion) so you autoregulate — pushing hard on good days and backing off when tired, " +
79	            "which the evidence links to better long-term gains and fewer injuries."
80	
81	        let safetyNotes: String
82	        if answers.injuries.isEmpty {
83	            safetyNotes =
84	                "Warm up before your first heavy set, keep one or two reps in reserve early in a " +
85	                "session, and prioritize sleep — that's when adaptation actually happens."
86	        } else {
87	            let list = answers.injuries.map(\.displayName).joined(separator: ", ")
88	            safetyNotes =
89	                "You told us about: \(list). We deliberately avoided loading those areas as primary " +
90	                "movers and chose joint-friendly alternatives. Stop any movement that causes sharp " +
91	                "pain and give those areas extra warm-up time."
92	        }
93	
94	        let encouragement =
95	            "\(greeting.capitalizedFirst)your health and consistency matter more than any single session — " +
96	            "show up, log your sets, and let the progress compound. We've got you."
97	
98	        return PlanReport(
99	            philosophy: philosophy,
100	            whyThisSplit: whyThisSplit,
101	            perDay: perDay,
102	            scienceNotes: scienceNotes,
103	            safetyNotes: safetyNotes,
104	            encouragement: encouragement
105	        )
106	    }
107	
108	    /// Convenience: a fully-rendered fallback markdown report.
109	    static func fallbackMarkdown(answers: QuizAnswers, plan: GeneratedPlan) -> String {
110	        markdown(report: fallbackReport(answers: answers, plan: plan), plan: plan)
111	    }
112	
113	    // MARK: - Helpers
114	
115	    /// Turns a catalog id ("Alternating_Floor_Press") into a display name ("Alternating Floor Press").
116	    static func prettyName(_ exId: String) -> String {
117	        exId.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: " ")
118	    }
119

121	        index == 0
122	            ? "Your primary compound lift for this day — the biggest driver of strength and size."
123	            : "Accessory work that adds focused volume and rounds out the day's stimulus."
124	    }

128	    /// Capitalizes only the first character (so "alex, we…" → "Alex, we…").

9	import Foundation

11	
12	enum ReplogSchema {
13	    /// All persisted model types.
14	    static let models: [any PersistentModel.Type] = [
15	        Plan.self, Workout.self, PlanItem.self, SetTemplate.self,
16	        ActiveSession.self, SessionExercise.self, LoggedSet.self,
17	        HistoryEntry.self, UserProfile.self, AppSettings.self,

21	    /// The app's on-disk container.
22	    /// On a fresh device install `Library/Application Support` may not exist yet, which
23	    /// makes SwiftData fail to create its store ("Failed to create file; code = 2"). We
24	    /// create that directory first, then open the store; if the store itself is corrupt
25	    /// or schema-incompatible (e.g. left over from an older build), we wipe it once and
26	    /// retry, falling back to in-memory as a last resort so the app always launches.
27	    @MainActor

30	        let config = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: false)

2	//  StreakEngine.swift
3	//  Replog
4	//
5	//  Schedule-aware streaks. Unlike a Duolingo daily streak, these are driven by the
6	//  user's *plan schedule* (which weekdays have a workout):
7	//
8	//   • Workout streak — consecutive scheduled workouts completed. A scheduled weekday
9	//     that ends without its workout done resets it to 0. Today's scheduled workout,
10	//     while still undone, does not break it (in-progress grace).
11	//
12	//   • Week streak — consecutive "perfect weeks" (every scheduled workout that week
13	//     completed). Because a missed workout breaks the workout streak, it also breaks
14	//     the week streak ("grouped inside"): the workout streak counts sessions, the week
15	//     streak counts whole weeks, and a single miss resets both.
16	//
17	//  All functions are pure (no SwiftData), so they're fully unit-testable.
18	//
19	
20	import Foundation
21	
22	enum StreakEngine {
23	
24	    /// Distinct weekdays that have at least one scheduled workout across the given plans.
25	    static func scheduledDays(in plans: [Plan]) -> Set<Weekday> {
26	        Set(plans.flatMap(\.workouts).map(\.day))
27	    }
28	
29	    /// Consecutive scheduled workouts completed, counting back from `today`.
30	    /// Stops at the first *past* scheduled weekday with no completion. A scheduled
31	    /// workout that is still due today (undone) is skipped, not counted as a miss.
32	    static func workoutStreak(
33	        scheduledDays: Set<Weekday>,
34	        doneDates: [Date],
35	        today: Date = Date(),
36	        calendar: Calendar = .current
37	    ) -> Int {
38	        guard !scheduledDays.isEmpty else { return 0 }
39	        let doneDays = Set(doneDates.map { calendar.startOfDay(for: $0) })
40	        guard !doneDays.isEmpty else { return 0 }
41	
42	        let startOfToday = calendar.startOfDay(for: today)
43	        var cursor = startOfToday
44	        var count = 0
45	        // Safety bound: never walk more than ~2 years of days.
46	        for _ in 0..<732 {
47	            let weekday = Weekday.from(cursor, calendar: calendar)
48	            if scheduledDays.contains(weekday) {
49	                if doneDays.contains(cursor) {
50	                    count += 1
51	                } else if cursor != startOfToday {
52	                    // A past scheduled workout was missed → streak ends here.
53	                    break
54	                }
55	                // else: today's scheduled workout is still due — grace, don't break.
56	            }
57	            guard let prev = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -1, to: cursor) else { break }
58	            cursor = prev
59	            // Once we're older than every completion, the next scheduled day is a miss.
60	            if let earliest = doneDays.min(), cursor < earliest { break }
61	        }
62	        return count
63	    }
64	
65	    /// Consecutive "perfect weeks" ending at the current week.
66	    ///
67	    /// • The current week counts as in-progress (+1) when every *elapsed* scheduled
68	    ///   workout (on or before today) is done and at least one has been done. If an
69	    ///   elapsed scheduled workout this week was missed, the whole streak is broken (0).
70	    /// • Each prior week counts only if *all* of its scheduled workouts were completed.
71	    static func weekStreak(
72	        scheduledDays: Set<Weekday>,
73	        doneDates: [Date],
74	        today: Date = Date(),
75	        calendar: Calendar = .current
76	    ) -> Int {
77	        guard !scheduledDays.isEmpty else { return 0 }
78	        let doneDays = Set(doneDates.map { calendar.startOfDay(for: $0) })
79	        let startOfToday = calendar.startOfDay(for: today)
80	        guard let thisWeekStart = startOfWeek(for: startOfToday, calendar: calendar) else { return 0 }
81	
82	        var weeks = 0
83	
84	        // Current (in-progress) week.
85	        let scheduledThisWeek = scheduledDates(weekStart: thisWeekStart, scheduledDays: scheduledDays, calendar: calendar)
86	        // A *past* scheduled workout (before today) left undone is a miss → breaks both streaks.
87	        // Today's scheduled workout, while still due, gets the same grace as the workout streak.
88	        let pastScheduled = scheduledThisWeek.filter { $0 < startOfToday }
89	        if pastScheduled.contains(where: { !doneDays.contains($0) }) {
90	            return 0
91	        }
92	        let doneThisWeek = scheduledThisWeek.filter { $0 <= startOfToday && doneDays.contains($0) }
93	        if !doneThisWeek.isEmpty {
94	            weeks += 1 // On track with at least one scheduled workout done.
95	        }
96	
97	        // Prior weeks: require every scheduled workout completed.
98	        guard var cursor = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -7, to: thisWeekStart) else { return weeks }
99	        for _ in 0..<104 { // ~2 years of weeks
100	            let scheduled = scheduledDates(weekStart: cursor, scheduledDays: scheduledDays, calendar: calendar)
101	            guard !scheduled.isEmpty, scheduled.allSatisfy({ doneDays.contains($0) }) else { break }
102	            weeks += 1
103	            guard let prev = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -7, to: cursor) else { break }
104	            cursor = prev
105	        }
106	        return weeks
107	    }
108	
109	    // MARK: - Helpers
110	
111	    /// The Sunday that starts the week containing `date` (matches the Today week strip).
112	    static func startOfWeek(for date: Date, calendar: Calendar = .current) -> Date? {
113	        let startOfDay = calendar.startOfDay(for: date)
114	        let weekdayIndex = calendar.component(.weekday, from: startOfDay) - 1 // 0 = Sunday
115	        return calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: -weekdayIndex, to: startOfDay)
116	    }
117	
118	    /// The concrete dates of the scheduled weekdays within the week starting `weekStart`.
119	    private static func scheduledDates(
120	        weekStart: Date,
121	        scheduledDays: Set<Weekday>,
122	        calendar: Calendar
123	    ) -> [Date] {
124	        (0..<7).compactMap { offset -> Date? in
125	            guard let date = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: offset, to: weekStart) else { return nil }
126	            return scheduledDays.contains(Weekday.from(date, calendar: calendar)) ? date : nil
127	        }
128	    }
129	}

2	//  BodyweightTracker.swift
3	//  Replog
4	//
5	//  Pure logic for the periodic bodyweight check-in: when the next check-in is due,
6	//  and the trend over the recent series (delta, weekly rate, direction). Storage is
7	//  `BodyweightEntry`; display conversion lives in `Formulas`.
8	//
9	
10	import Foundation
11	
12	/// A digest of the recent bodyweight series, ready for the Today card.
13	struct BodyweightSnapshot: Equatable, Sendable {
14	    /// The latest logged weight, in kg.
15	    var currentKg: Double
16	    /// When it was logged.
17	    var date: Date
18	    /// Change vs the previous check-in, in kg (nil for the first entry).
19	    var deltaKg: Double?
20	    /// Least-squares rate of change over the trailing window, in kg per week
21	    /// (nil until two check-ins land inside the window).
22	    var weeklyRateKg: Double?
23	    /// Direction of `weeklyRateKg` with a noise deadband (`.none` while rate is nil).
24	    var direction: Trend
25	    /// The recent series (oldest first) scaled for `Sparkline`'s integer values.
26	    var sparklineValues: [Int]
27	}
28	
29	enum BodyweightTracker {
30	
31	    /// Days between check-in prompts.
32	    static let checkInIntervalDays = 7
33	    /// Trailing window the weekly rate is fitted over.
34	    static let trendWindowDays = 28
35	    /// |rate| below this reads as scale noise, not a trend (kg per week).
36	    static let flatBandKgPerWeek = 0.15
37	    /// How many recent entries the sparkline shows.
38	    static let sparklinePoints = 12
39	
40	    /// Whether the periodic check-in is due: no entry yet, or the last one is at least
41	    /// `checkInIntervalDays` calendar days old.
42	    static func checkInDue(lastDate: Date?, now: Date = Date(),
43	                           calendar: Calendar = .current) -> Bool {
44	        guard let lastDate else { return true }
45	        let from = calendar.startOfDay(for: lastDate)
46	        let to = calendar.startOfDay(for: now)
47	        let days = calendar.dateComponents([.day], from: from, to: to).day ?? 0
48	        return days >= checkInIntervalDays
49	    }
50	
51	    /// Digests the series into the Today-card snapshot. Order-invariant; nil when empty.
52	    @MainActor
53	    static func snapshot(entries: [BodyweightEntry]) -> BodyweightSnapshot? {
54	        let sorted = entries.sorted { $0.date < $1.date }
55	        guard let latest = sorted.last else { return nil }
56	
57	        let previous = sorted.dropLast().last
58	        let rate = weeklyRate(sorted: sorted, anchoredAt: latest.date)
59	
60	        return BodyweightSnapshot(
61	            currentKg: latest.weightKg,
62	            date: latest.date,
63	            deltaKg: previous.map { latest.weightKg - $0.weightKg },
64	            weeklyRateKg: rate,
65	            direction: direction(weeklyRateKg: rate),
66	            // 0.1 kg resolution — Sparkline normalises, so only relative shape matters.
67	            sparklineValues: sorted.suffix(sparklinePoints).map { Int(($0.weightKg * 10).rounded()) }
68	        )
69	    }
70	
71	    /// Whether a trend direction moves toward (`true`), against (`false`), or neutrally
72	    /// (nil) with respect to the user's goal. Drives the card tint only — flat is always
73	    /// neutral, and recomp/sport have no "right" direction for the scale.
74	    static func isFavorable(_ direction: Trend, for goal: Goal) -> Bool? {
75	        switch (direction, goal) {
76	        case (.up, .buildMuscle): return true
77	        case (.up, .loseWeight): return false
78	        case (.down, .loseWeight): return true
79	        case (.down, .buildMuscle): return false
80	        default: return nil
81	        }
82	    }
83	
84	    // MARK: - Internals
85	
86	    /// Least-squares slope (kg/week) over entries within `trendWindowDays` of the anchor.
87	    @MainActor
88	    private static func weeklyRate(sorted: [BodyweightEntry], anchoredAt anchor: Date) -> Double? {
89	        let windowStart = anchor.addingTimeInterval(-Double(trendWindowDays) * 86_400)
90	        let window = sorted.filter { $0.date >= windowStart }
91	        guard window.count >= 2 else { return nil }
92	
93	        let days = window.map { $0.date.timeIntervalSince(windowStart) / 86_400 }
94	        let weights = window.map(\.weightKg)
95	        let n = Double(window.count)
96	        let meanX = days.reduce(0.0, +) / n
97	        let meanY = weights.reduce(0.0, +) / n
98	        var covXY = 0.0
99	        var varX = 0.0
100	        for (x, y) in zip(days, weights) {
101	            covXY += (x - meanX) * (y - meanY)
102	            varX += (x - meanX) * (x - meanX)
103	        }
104	        // All entries on the same day (upsert makes this rare): no time spread, no rate.
105	        guard varX > 0 else { return nil }
106	        return covXY / varX * 7
107	    }
108	
109	    private static func direction(weeklyRateKg: Double?) -> Trend {
110	        guard let rate = weeklyRateKg else { return .none }
111	        if rate > flatBandKgPerWeek { return .up }
112	        if rate < -flatBandKgPerWeek { return .down }
113	        return .flat
114	    }
115	}
